faq.a: Abdulhamid represents Arabic عَبْدُ الْحَمِيد, meaning servant of the Praiseworthy.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulhamid?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْحَمِيد (ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdulhamid?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-Ḥamīd is related to ح م د (ḥ-m-d).
Abdulhamid is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Ḥamīd, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdulhamid as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the Praiseworthy; the compound combines عبد with al-Ḥamīd.
The supplied “ab-dul-ha-mid” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
